## Solution

We are given
$$
u_{xt}(x,t)+u(x,t)\,u_{xx}(x,t)=h(t),\qquad x\in[0,\pi],\ t>0,
$$
with boundary conditions
$$
u(\pi,t)=0,\qquad u_x(0,t)=0,\qquad u_x(\pi,t)=0\quad\text{for all }t>0.
$$

All necessary regularity is assumed, so the PDE holds up to the boundary and the boundary data may be differentiated in $t$.

**Key observation.** The boundary condition $u_x(\pi,t)=0$ holds for every $t>0$. Differentiating it with respect to $t$ gives
$$
u_{xt}(\pi,t)=0\qquad\text{for all }t>0. \tag{1}
$$

The boundary condition $u(\pi,t)=0$ also holds for every $t>0$, hence
$$
u(\pi,t)=0\qquad\text{for all }t>0. \tag{2}
$$

**Evaluate the PDE at $x=\pi$.** Since the PDE is satisfied on $[0,\pi]$ (regularity assumed), we may set $x=\pi$:
$$
u_{xt}(\pi,t)+u(\pi,t)\,u_{xx}(\pi,t)=h(t). \tag{3}
$$

Substituting (1) and (2) into (3):
$$
0 + 0\cdot u_{xx}(\pi,t)=h(t),
$$
that is,
$$
h(t)=0.
$$

**Consistency check at $x=0$.** Differentiating $u_x(0,t)=0$ in $t$ gives $u_{xt}(0,t)=0$. Evaluating the PDE at $x=0$:
$$
u_{xt}(0,t)+u(0,t)\,u_{xx}(0,t)=h(t)\;\Longrightarrow\;u(0,t)\,u_{xx}(0,t)=0,
$$
which is consistent with $h(t)=0$ (it forces either $u(0,t)=0$ or $u_{xx}(0,t)=0$ at the left endpoint, both compatible with the homogeneous boundary data).

**Why three boundary conditions pin down $h(t)$.** The equation is second order in $x$ (the term $u\,u_{xx}$ is second order), so two boundary conditions would normally suffice. The third condition $u_x(\pi,t)=0$ is an *overdetermination*: combined with $u(\pi,t)=0$ it forces, via the PDE evaluated at $x=\pi$, the otherwise-free function $h(t)$ to vanish. This is exactly the mechanism exhibited above.

Therefore the function $h(t)$ is identically zero:

$$
\boxed{\,h(t)=0\,}.
$$
